source.title: ArchDaily project page 'Elementary School in Tel Aviv / Auerbach Halevy Architects': first-floor plan (TLV_school_-_First_Floor.jpg, 2000 x 1255 px, no scale bar), ground-floor plan and section 1
source.license: Published plan, used only as a reference for dimensions

meta.scale: 23.1 px/m, about +-6 %. Anchor: the south-east classroom's inner depth (160 px) = 7.0 m, the dimensioned depth of the Ministry of Education M21 classroom (meyda.education.gov.il M21models.pdf p.19). Checks at this scale: stair treads 6.8 px = 0.30 m; door swings 0.85 m; section 1 (same pixel width as the plan) gives a ground-floor storey of 3.9 m and 5.7 m from the first floor to the corridor roof.
assumptions: Scale 23.1 px/m (+-6 %) from the M21 classroom depth, cross-checked by stair treads, door swings and the section's storey height; every length scales with it
Box 68.9 x 32.0 m = the whole first floor's bounding rectangle (plan px 237-1829 x 258-997)
Height 5.6 m = first floor to the corridor roof soffit read from section 1; classroom ceilings 3.3 m assumed (below the 4.1 m clerestory sill)
South-west wing is drawn rotated about 10 degrees; squared here about its centre, keeping its classroom sizes (15.0 x 7.0 m for S1 + S2)

Protected space inferred, not labelled on the plan: the science lab is the only classroom-size room with 0.30-0.45 m walls on all four sides, entered through a two-door lobby, and the same room repeats on the ground floor (protected spaces stack). In a school this is a mamam (institutional protected space), not a residential mamak. Net area 58 m2 between wall faces (65 m2 to wall centre lines), close to the 60 m2 per-space limit the council cited (s.236), within the scale error

Against the protected-space reading: the plan shows three 1.1 m windows in the lab's north wall (residential rules allow one window of at most 1.21 m2, a mamak none); modelled as mamad_glazing (steel leaves open, daily use)

Lab walls mamad_30 (44 dB at 5 GHz) on all sides: mamam rules ask 30 cm outside and 25 cm inside above 20 m2, and every side is drawn 0.30 m or thicker; blast door between the lobby and the lab open, as in daily use. The lobby's corridor door sits at plan y 523 as drawn
Staff suite (south-east) has 0.30 m walls towards the commons and classroom S4: modelled as RC concrete_25 (25 cm core plus plaster), not claimed as a protected space
Facades: plastered 20 cm block (block_20) drawn 0.30 m with insulation; the ArchDaily page lists concrete, wood and steel only
Stair core concrete_25 (drawn 0.35-0.39 m); lift shaft concrete_20; classroom party walls block_20; toilets and small rooms block_10
N1 / N2 folding partition modelled as wood; classroom fronts onto the corridor and commons are glass (section 1 shows glazed fronts with double doors)
Windows: uncoated double glazing, sill 0.9 m, height 1.5 m (toilets: high 0.6 m windows); no trisim, the south rooms are shaded by fixed precast fins (not modelled)

Light wells along the corridor, the stair opening and the library roof are voids with no floor on this level: labelled outside, left out of the shares; their glass balustrades are 1.1 m high (open above; Israeli rule of thumb for public-building guards, not read from the plan)
Room uses read from the drawn furniture; 'activity room' and 'prep room' names are assumed (group tables, sinks, kiln-like box)
Communications cabinet assumed in the closet of the staff-suite lobby
AP1 on the corridor ceiling between the N1 / N2 doors and bridge 1 (z 5.4 m, 5 GHz, 20 dBm): where an installer would put the first one; not shown on the plan
Fire doors of the stair hall held open; classroom doors closed
Desks, tables and sofas are drawn but have no radio loss; up to 40 pupils per classroom (20 double desks drawn; body loss) are not modelled
israeli_features: Mamam (institutional protected space) inferred in the science lab: RC walls, blast door and a two-door entry lobby; used as a classroom every day
Ministry-of-Education classrooms of about 50 m2 for 40 pupils (20 double desks), paired, with 'learning commons' between them
High central corridor (5.6 m) with clerestory windows and light wells to the ground floor
Separate boys' and girls' toilets, an accessible WC and a cleaner's store
Teachers' room with a kitchenette and a lounge corner
meta.notes: A 2015 Tel Aviv primary school: a long, high corridor with classrooms on both sides, two courtyard wings and a teachers' wing at the west end. One ceiling AP in the corridor reaches the glass-fronted classrooms N1 and N2 and the corridor, but the 44 dB walls of the lab (the inferred mamam), the concrete stair core and the block party walls leave the far wings with little or no service. Readings far below -100 dBm are an artefact of straight-line paths (the model has no diffraction or corridor guiding); read them as 'no service'. A real school needs about one AP per classroom.
